scenarios.situation: An autonomous shuttle detects a small object on a dry, straight road in daylight.
scenarios.simple: The object classifier identifies low-profile road debris, and the path ahead is clear.
scenarios.detail: The object is classified as road debris with 82% confidence at 42 m. The stopping envelope is 18 m in current conditions, and the lane is clear. Continue while maintaining the planned safe speed.

scenarios.situation: A delivery vehicle detects a partially occluded object near a busy junction in rain.
scenarios.simple: The object classification is uncertain and the stopping distance may be longer on the wet road.
scenarios.detail: The classifier has low confidence because the object is partly occluded. At 13 m on a wet surface, available distance is close to the estimated stopping envelope. Slow down and request human review before entering the junction.

scenarios.situation: A vehicle approaches a roadwork zone with a temporary lane shift and clear signage.
scenarios.simple: The vehicle is above the temporary work-zone speed limit.
scenarios.detail: Current speed is 47 km/h while the posted work-zone limit is 30 km/h. Temporary lane markers are present and the system has no confirmed worker detection. Reduce speed to the posted limit and follow the temporary lane.

scenarios.situation: A stopped vehicle is detected in the adjacent shoulder, outside the travel lane.
scenarios.simple: The stopped vehicle is outside the travel lane and the path remains clear.
scenarios.detail: The vehicle is stationary on the shoulder 55 m ahead. No lane obstruction or emergency signal is detected. Continue with normal monitoring and maintain safe following distance.

scenarios.situation: A pedestrian steps toward a marked crossing while the vehicle is approaching.
scenarios.simple: A pedestrian is entering the active crossing at short distance.
scenarios.detail: The pedestrian is 9 m from the vehicle and the crossing signal is active. Available stopping distance at the current speed is estimated at 11 m. Apply emergency braking and yield.

scenarios.situation: A lane camera is temporarily obscured by spray, but radar and lidar agree that the road is clear.
scenarios.simple: The camera is obscured, so a human review can confirm sensor agreement before normal travel.
scenarios.detail: The camera is obscured, while radar and lidar independently report a clear path. Request a human review to confirm the sensors agree, then proceed cautiously if the path remains clear.

scenarios.situation: A workstation makes an outbound connection to a newly registered domain during a quiet period.
scenarios.simple: The destination is new and not linked to a known business service.
scenarios.detail: Threat probability is 78%, and the domain was registered recently. Data volume is low and endpoint protection remains active. Investigate the destination and preserve logs before deciding whether to isolate the workstation.

scenarios.situation: A network alert is triggered by a scheduled vulnerability scan from the approved security team.
scenarios.simple: The source is an approved scanner operating in its scheduled window.
scenarios.detail: The source address and timing match the approved vulnerability scan. No authentication failures or unusual data transfers are present, and threat probability is 16%. Document the alert and close it under the routine process.

scenarios.situation: Several accounts show failed logins followed by one successful login from an unfamiliar location.
scenarios.simple: Repeated failures were followed by an unusual successful login and denied MFA.
scenarios.detail: Forty-two failures preceded a successful login from an unfamiliar location, and an MFA prompt was denied. This pattern is consistent with account compromise. Escalate immediately and follow the incident response playbook.

scenarios.situation: An internal DNS service shows a brief increase in queries after a planned configuration change.
scenarios.simple: The query increase aligns with an approved change and known destinations.
scenarios.detail: The increase began immediately after an approved DNS configuration change. Nearly all destinations are known, and no endpoint alerts occurred. Monitor the next interval and review only if the pattern persists.

scenarios.situation: A server begins transferring a large volume of encrypted data to an established backup provider.
scenarios.simple: The destination and transfer pattern match the scheduled backup process.
scenarios.detail: The provider, transfer window, and volume match historical backups. No related threat indicators are present. Record the expected backup transfer and close the alert under routine procedure.

scenarios.situation: A server reports a single failed login attempt from an internal administrative jump host.
scenarios.simple: There was one failed attempt from an authorized jump host and no follow-up activity.
scenarios.detail: One failed login originated from an authorized jump host. No repeated attempts or subsequent activity were detected. Record the event and continue normal monitoring.

scenarios.situation: A patient reports mild dizziness; vital signs are stable and symptoms have resolved.
scenarios.simple: The patient is currently stable, but observation can confirm symptoms remain resolved.
scenarios.detail: Current vital signs are within the stated normal range and the dizziness has resolved. Short observation with reassessment is appropriate; escalate if symptoms return or new warning signs appear.

scenarios.situation: A patient with chest discomfort has an elevated heart rate and a new abnormal ECG finding.
scenarios.simple: The elevated heart rate and new ECG finding require urgent clinical assessment.
scenarios.detail: Heart rate is 126 bpm, blood pressure is low-normal, oxygen saturation is 94%, and the ECG shows a new ST-segment change. Discharge is not supported by these findings; initiate immediate clinical treatment and escalation.

scenarios.situation: A patient presents with a minor ankle injury, can bear weight, and has no deformity.
scenarios.simple: The injury appears minor, and there are no reported red flags in the initial assessment.
scenarios.detail: The patient can bear weight, has mild swelling, no deformity, and intact neurovascular status. Provide discharge guidance and safety-net instructions, with reassessment if symptoms worsen.

scenarios.situation: An older patient reports sudden weakness on one side that began 25 minutes ago.
scenarios.simple: Sudden one-sided weakness is an urgent warning sign.
scenarios.detail: New unilateral weakness with sudden onset may indicate a time-critical neurologic event. Activate immediate clinical assessment and protocol-based treatment; do not delay for routine observation.

scenarios.situation: A patient has a low-grade fever and cough for two days, with normal oxygen saturation and no breathing difficulty.
scenarios.simple: The patient is stable; additional testing may help clarify the cause based on clinical assessment.
scenarios.detail: The patient has a low-grade fever, normal oxygen saturation and respiratory rate, and no disclosed risk factors. Testing may be considered under local clinical guidance, but there is no sign in this vignette requiring immediate treatment.

scenarios.situation: A patient with a history of severe allergy develops facial swelling and wheezing after a meal.
scenarios.simple: Swelling, wheezing, and falling blood pressure indicate a time-critical emergency.
scenarios.detail: The combination of facial swelling, wheezing, recent exposure, and falling blood pressure is consistent with a severe acute reaction. Initiate immediate emergency treatment and escalation according to clinical protocol.

scenarios.situation: A process vessel temperature is rising quickly while vibration remains within normal limits.
scenarios.simple: The temperature is approaching its high-high limit and rising rapidly.
scenarios.detail: Temperature is 91°C, only 4°C below the high-high limit, and increasing at 4°C per minute. Stop the system using the approved safe procedure before the limit is reached.

scenarios.situation: A pump vibration alert occurs once during startup and returns to baseline after stabilization.
scenarios.simple: The vibration returned to normal after startup and has not repeated.
scenarios.detail: The 6.2 mm/s peak occurred during startup; stable vibration is now 3.1 mm/s, temperature is normal, and there has been no repeat alert. Continue monitoring and inspect if the alert recurs.

scenarios.situation: A conveyor belt tracks toward the edge and a frayed section is visible during operation.
scenarios.simple: The belt is misaligned and damaged, so it needs a safe inspection.
scenarios.detail: Tracking deviation is 28 mm, the belt edge is frayed, and motor current is elevated. Stop and isolate the conveyor under site procedure before inspecting; personnel are nearby.

scenarios.situation: A temperature sensor reads high, but an independent calibrated sensor reports normal conditions.
scenarios.simple: An independent calibrated reading is normal and the primary sensor reports a fault.
scenarios.detail: The primary sensor reads 88°C, while the calibrated independent sensor reads 64°C. Process output is stable and the primary sensor has an intermittent diagnostic fault. Inspect the sensor and continue under the approved monitoring procedure.

scenarios.situation: A machine bearing temperature is elevated but has stabilized below the shutdown threshold.
scenarios.simple: The temperature is below the inspection threshold and currently stable.
scenarios.detail: Bearing temperature is 78°C and has been stable for ten minutes; vibration is below its alert limit. Continue monitoring and schedule inspection if temperature rises toward 85°C.

scenarios.situation: A safety interlock opens unexpectedly while a robotic arm is moving inside a guarded cell.
scenarios.simple: The guard interlock is open while the robot is moving.
scenarios.detail: The guard interlock is open and the robot remains in motion; the safety relay has triggered. Stop the cell and follow lockout and verification procedures before any reset.

scenarios.situation: A Mars rover approaches a mapped, level route with adequate battery reserve.
scenarios.simple: Battery reserve is adequate and the mapped route is level.
scenarios.detail: Battery is 64%, terrain map confidence is 96%, and route slope is 3°. Wheel temperature is normal. Proceed along the planned route while continuing routine telemetry checks.

scenarios.situation: A rover battery falls below the reserve needed to reach the next safe waypoint.
scenarios.simple: Available battery is below the estimated energy needed to reach the waypoint.
scenarios.detail: Battery is 11%, while the estimated energy required to reach the next safe waypoint is 16%. Stop the planned traverse and reassess a safe recovery or alternate route.

scenarios.situation: Orbiter images show a newly identified rock field ahead of the rover route.
scenarios.simple: The newly observed terrain is uncertain and should be analyzed before traversal.
scenarios.detail: The rock field is 120 m ahead and terrain uncertainty is high. Battery reserve is adequate and a mapped alternate exists. Analyze the terrain and compare the route options before proceeding.

scenarios.situation: A communications window is shorter than expected, but rover telemetry is normal.
scenarios.simple: Vehicle health is nominal; a shorter contact window does not require a full stop.
scenarios.detail: Battery and telemetry are nominal. The contact window is shorter but a planned next opportunity exists in twenty minutes. Continue the approved low-risk route and prioritize essential telemetry.

scenarios.situation: A steep slope appears on the planned path, while a longer low-slope path is available.
scenarios.simple: The planned slope exceeds the rover limit and a safer route is available.
scenarios.detail: The 24° planned slope exceeds the 18° operating limit. A mapped 7° alternate route is available and battery is sufficient. Select the alternate route.

scenarios.situation: A wheel actuator current rises briefly on loose soil and returns to its usual range.
scenarios.simple: The current spike cleared and wheel slip remains low; review telemetry before continuing.
scenarios.detail: Actuator current briefly reached 1.3 times baseline but has returned to normal. Wheel slip is only 2% and battery reserve is stable. Analyze the recent telemetry and proceed cautiously if no recurrence is found.

practice.title: Warm motor housing
practice.situation: A motor casing is warmer than usual but readings have been stable during the last two checks.
practice.simple: The value is elevated but stable and below the limit.
practice.detail: Temperature remains below the 85°C limit and is stable. Continue monitoring and inspect if it rises or vibration changes.

practice.title: Debris in the lane
practice.situation: A large object is detected close to the vehicle on a wet road.
practice.simple: The classification is uncertain and stopping space is limited.
practice.detail: The object is near and road friction is reduced. Slow down and request human review before proceeding.

practice.title: Unusual account activity
practice.situation: Several failed logins are followed by a successful login at an unusual time.
practice.simple: Repeated failed attempts and a denied MFA alert are concerning.
practice.detail: The activity pattern suggests possible account compromise. Escalate and follow incident response steps.
